docs.dcterms_abstract: Love to Margaret and Bridget. Elizabeth Corte (Cowart) remembers her love to everyone there and to Thomas Benson and his wife. Suggests that they are being dishonorable and disobedient and hopefully Fell's prayers will straighten them out. Corte (Cowart) and Newby went to Homisham and had a meeting in Genyworthe. Fox was in Tewksbury. Corte (Cowart) and Newby are going to Bristol to see the 'Two Johns' (John Story and John Wilkinson). docs.dcterms_abstract: John Audland has travelled a lot—Oxford and Banbury, then Wales. Francis Howgill and Edward Burrough were with him in Bristol, but they went back to London. Thomas Robertson is free. Few in Lancston. Some in jail in Exeter, including Nayler—who is much as he was. John Poulton wrote to JA the following: Nayler is the same as before. Names of Exeter prisoners—twenty-three in all:  John Boulton, James Nayler, Nicholas Ganecliffe, Thomas Rawlinson, Thomas Bylston, Henry Goodman, John James, Roberta Crabb, Samwell Cator, Thomas Rawkings, John Browne, Thomas Powel, William Bayle, Humphrey Smith, Priscilla Cottten, Ratterance Martin Dall, Jane Bland, Ann Rawlinson, Mary Erbery, Dorcas Erbery, Elizabeth Catland, Joan Ingram, and Katherine Thorne in Bridewell.

docs.dcterms_abstract: Priscilla Cotton is home in Plymouth and is refreshed. John Brechet was in Plymouth but went into Cornwall where he had several meetings, one at Stokeny Lansiston. First meeting there. Truth spreads and friends are 'obegant'. R. Vicksander was with them but he went away. TS [Thomas Salthouse?] is with us. Meeting in Sardis increases. Barbara Pattison was with them but she went to Bristol. George Buly is still in Cornwall.

docs.dcterms_abstract: Ann Dewsbury sends Fell a copy of some passages from her husband—his work and travels. Since William Dewsbury left Lands End in Cornwall he is been in service—had a meeting at Humray Lowar’s house—then went to a meeting at Lanceston and another in Devonshire. Then he met up with some men in Terinton where he was accused of being a Jesuit for not taking the oath of Abjuration. Ann and his children visited William Dewsbury in Cornwall. In jail in Exeter. Once out, he went to Somersetshire and had a meeting with Thomas Salthouse and the rest in prison. Then a meeting in Wiltshire. Then one at Justice Cripte’s house in Gloucestershire, then Slettinford, then Bristol. Since sending this Ann received one a letter from her husband which was written from prison—he says friends are in jail there and William Dewsbury was going to Wales soon.
